extracted.intended_audience: immigration attorneys, employers petitioning for nonimmigrant workers, and nonimmigrant visa applicants/beneficiaries
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and adjudication standards governing H-, I-, and J-class nonimmigrants: exceptions to residence rules, petition and stay extension procedures and limits, fees and exemptions, strike/retaliation effects, portability for H-2B workers, media and exchange visitor obligations, and related procedural documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to immediate prior 6-month residence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The limitations that an alien must have resided and been physically present outside the United States for the immediate prior 6 months will not apply to H-1B and H-3 aliens who did not reside continually in the United States and whose employment was seasonal or intermittent or for an aggregate of 6 months or less per year; nor to aliens who reside abroad and regularly commute to the United States to engage in part-time employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To qualify for this exception, the petitioner and the alien must provide clear and convincing proof such as arrival/departure records, copies of tax returns, and records of employment abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of visa petition validity (Form I-129)
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must file a request for a petition extension on Form I-129 to extend the validity of the original petition under section 101(a)(15)(H) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for a petition extension generally may be filed only if the validity of the original petition has not expired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of stay — general filing and adjudication rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner shall apply for extension of an alien's stay by filing a petition extension on the form prescribed by USCIS accompanied by required documents; the beneficiary must be physically present in the United States at time of filing; petitioner must also request a petition extension; dates of extension are the same for the petition and beneficiary's extension of stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director makes separate determinations on petition and extension of stay. If the alien must depart while extension requests are pending, petitioner may request cabled notification of petition approval to consular office abroad. When total permitted H classification period is reached, no further extensions may be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1C extension limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum period of admission for an H-1C alien is 3 years; an H-1C alien initially admitted for less than 3 years may receive an extension up to the third anniversary date of initial admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An H-1C nonimmigrant may not receive an extension of stay beyond the third anniversary date of initial admission.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1B extension periods and total stay limit (specialty occupations and fashion modeling)
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of stay may be authorized for up to three years for an H-1B beneficiary in a specialty occupation or an alien of distinguished merit and ability in fashion modeling; the alien's total period of stay may not exceed six years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request for extension must be accompanied by either a new or a photocopy of the prior Department of Labor certification (labor condition application) valid for the period requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1B extension for DOD R&D or coproduction projects
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of stay may be authorized for a period up to five years for an H-1B beneficiary involved in a DOD research and development or coproduction project; the total period of stay may not exceed 10 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2A and H-2B extension periods and total stay limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of stay for H-2A or H-2B beneficiaries may be authorized for the validity of the labor certification or for up to one year; the alien's total period of stay as an H-2A or H-2B worker may not exceed three years (except in the Virgin Islands where total stay may not exceed 45 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See paragraph (h)(5)(x) for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-3 extension of stay (trainees and special education participants)
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of stay may be authorized for the length of the training program for a total period of stay as an H-3 trainee not to exceed two years, or for a participant in a special education training program not to exceed 18 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of permanent labor certification or preference petition on H-1B/H-1C
rubrics_metrics.description: The approval of a permanent labor certification or the filing of a preference petition shall not be a basis for denying an H-1C or H-1B petition or a request to extend such a petition, or the alien's admission, change of status, or extension of stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The alien may legitimately be in H-1C/H-1B status temporarily while lawfully seeking permanent residence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of permanent labor certification or preference petition on H-2A/H-2B
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval or filing of a permanent labor certification, an immediate relative or preference petition, diversity visa petition, or application to seek lawful permanent residence will not, standing alone, be the basis for denying an H-2 petition, extension, admission, change of status, or extension of stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such filings will be considered with all other facts in determining whether the H-2 nonimmigrant is maintaining H-2 status and whether the alien has a foreign residence he/she does not intend to abandon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of permanent labor certification or preference petition on H-3
rubrics_metrics.description: The approval of a permanent labor certification, or the filing of a preference petition for an alien currently employed by or in a training position with the same petitioner, will be a reason, by itself, to deny the alien's extension of stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of strike — certified labor dispute
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Secretary of Labor certifies that a strike or other labor dispute involving a work stoppage is in progress in the occupation and at the place where the beneficiary is to be employed or trained and that the employment/training would adversely affect wages and working conditions of U.S. workers, a petition to classify an alien as H nonimmigrant shall be denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petition already approved but alien has not yet entered or commenced employment, the approval is automatically suspended and application for admission shall be denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of strike — uncertified labor dispute
rubrics_metrics.description: If a strike or other labor dispute involving a work stoppage is in progress but is not certified under the referenced paragraph, the Commissioner shall not deny a petition or suspend an approved petition on that basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of strike — participating employee protections and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien who has commenced employment under an approved petition and is participating in a strike/work stoppage shall not be deemed to be failing to maintain status solely for participation in the strike, but remains subject to all INA provisions and regulations; status and authorized period of stay are not modified or extended by participation; participation is not a ground for deportation, but violating status or overstaying may lead to deportation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of approval notice Form I-797
rubrics_metrics.description: The Service shall notify the petitioner on Form I-797 whenever a visa petition, extension of a visa petition, or an alien's extension of stay is approved under the H classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A beneficiary who does not require a nonimmigrant visa may present a copy at a port of entry to facilitate entry. A beneficiary with an expired visa may use Form I-797 to apply for a new or revalidated visa during the petition validity period. Retain and present Form I-797 during validity when reentering to resume same employment with same petitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACWIA additional fee — when required
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. employer (other than exempt employers or certain filing categories) who files a petition must include the additional American Competitiveness and Workforce Improvement Act (ACWIA) fee if the petition is filed for: (A) an initial grant of H-1B status; (B) an initial extension of stay; or (C) authorization for a change in employers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions and exceptions are specified in following paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACWIA fee payment and who may pay
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner must submit the ACWIA fee and any other applicable fees in accordance with §103.7 and form instructions; payment of all applicable fees must be made at the same time though separate checks may be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will accept ACWIA fee only from the United States employer or its representative of record as defined in 8 CFR 103.2(a) and 8 CFR part 292.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACWIA fee exemptions — qualifying organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Exempt organizations that are not required to pay the additional fee include: (A) an institution of higher education; (B) an affiliated or related nonprofit entity meeting specified affiliation/operation/attachment/affiliation agreement criteria; (C) a nonprofit research organization or government research organization; (D) a primary or secondary education institution; and (E) a nonprofit entity engaging in curriculum-related clinical training of students registered at an institution of higher education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed conditions for affiliated/related nonprofit entity and research organization definitions are provided (e.g., IRS tax-exempt status for nonprofits).

rubrics_metrics.name: ACWIA fee exemption — nonprofit and governmental research organization definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprofit research organization or government research organization is defined by whether a fundamental activity is engaging in basic and/or applied research; government research orgs may be Federal, State, or local entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic research and applied research are defined. Organizations may perform/promote more than one fundamental activity; examples of research activities described.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACWIA fee — IRS tax-exempt status requirement for certain exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of certain nonprofit exemptions, a nonprofit organization or entity must be determined by the IRS to be tax exempt under Internal Revenue Code section 501(c)(3), (c)(4), or (c)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing situations where ACWIA fee is not required
rubrics_metrics.description: The ACWIA fee is not required if: (A) the petition is an amended H-1B petition that does not contain any requests for an extension of stay; (B) the petition is filed solely to correct a Service error; or (C) the petition is the second or subsequent request for an extension of stay filed by the employer regardless of timing or prior payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACWIA fee exemption evidence — employer burden
rubrics_metrics.description: An employer claiming exemption must file the form prescribed by USCIS with supporting evidence establishing the claimed exemption; a nonprofit research organization must submit evidence of tax-exempt status under 26 U.S.C. 501(c)(3),(c)(4),(c)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-exempt employers claiming a specific filing situation where the fee does not apply must indicate why the ACWIA fee is not required for that filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retaliatory action claims and extraordinary circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: If credible documentary evidence supports that a beneficiary faced retaliatory action from their employer based on reporting violations of labor condition application obligations, USCIS may consider loss/failure to maintain H-1B status as due to 'extraordinary circumstances' as defined by relevant CFR provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, for H-2A/H-2B, credible evidence that beneficiary faced retaliation based on a reasonable claim of violation or engagement in protected activity may lead USCIS to consider loss/failure to maintain status as due to extraordinary circumstances; USCIS will determine reasonableness from the perspective of a reasonable person in the worker's position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: If any revisions effective on a listed date to specified paragraphs are held invalid or unenforceable, they should be construed to continue to give maximum effect permitted by law; wholly invalid provisions should be severed without affecting other provisions or their application to persons/circumstances not similarly situated.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2B change of employers/portability (Jan 25, 2024 authorization window)
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien in valid H-2B nonimmigrant status whose new petitioner files a non-frivolous H-2B petition requesting an extension on or after Jan 25, 2024 is authorized to begin employment with the new petitioner after the petition is received by USCIS and before approval, but not earlier than the start date indicated in the petition. Similar authorization applies to petitions filed before Jan 25, 2024 but pending on that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding paragraph (h)(2)(i)(D). Specific subparagraphs set conditions and dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2B portability — new employment period up to 60 days
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to qualifying new petitions, the new period of employment may last for up to 60 days beginning on the Received Date on Form I-797 or, if the start date occurs after the I-797 Received Date, for up to 60 days beginning on the start date indicated in the H-2B petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2B portability — termination upon denial or withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: If USCIS adjudicates the new petition before the 60-day period expires and denies the petition, or if the new petition is withdrawn by the petitioner before expiration, the employment authorization associated with the filing will automatically terminate 15 days after the date of denial or withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2B portability — professional athletes exception note
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the portability paragraph is intended to alter the availability of employment authorization related to professional H-2B athletes who are traded between organizations pursuant to other specified paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2B portability — additional eligibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To commence employment under the portability provision, in addition to meeting other H-2B requirements, the alien must either (1) have been in valid H-2B status on/after Jan 25, 2024 and be beneficiary of a non-frivolous petition received on/after Jan 25, 2024 but no later than Jan 24, 2025; or (2) be beneficiary of a non-frivolous petition pending as of Jan 25, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petitioner may not impede, interfere, or refuse to cooperate with a DOL employee exercising audit/investigative authority under specified CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2B portability — authorization effective dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorization to initiate employment changes pursuant to the provision begins at 12 a.m. on Jan 25, 2024 and ends at the end of Jan 24, 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2B portability — subsequent authorization window (Jan 25, 2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analogous portability rules apply for petitions filed on or after Jan 25, 2025 (paragraph h(32)), authorizing employment after receipt and before approval, with analogous 60-day periods and termination rules, and requiring compliance with 8 CFR 274a.12(b)(35).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility windows and dates are Jan 25, 2025 through Jan 24, 2026 for that paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representatives of information media (I) — change of medium/employer agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Admission of an information media nonimmigrant constitutes agreement by the alien not to change the information medium or employer until permission is obtained from the district director having jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I nonimmigrant may be admitted for the duration of employment, except special PRC passport rule (see next).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representatives of information media (I) — PRC passport maximum period and Secretary's determination
rubrics_metrics.description: For aliens who present a passport issued by the People's Republic of China (other than HKSAR or Macao SAR passports), admission may be until activities/assignments are completed but not to exceed the maximum period determined by the Secretary (no longer than one year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In determining maximum period and whether adjustment is needed, the Secretary will consider factors including average authorized period of stay and press credential validity for U.S. journalists in the PRC, treatment of U.S. journalists in the PRC, input from the Department of State, and other factors affecting U.S. interest; such determination published in Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: I-status extension of stay and change of status procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: An I-status alien described in the PRC-passport paragraph may be eligible for extensions of stay each up to the maximum period determined by the Secretary or until activities are completed. To request an extension or change to I status, file the designated USCIS form with required fee and any biometrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests adjudicated consistent with international legal obligations such as the UN HQ and OAS HQ Agreements. A timely-filed extension allows continued employment and stay for up to 90 days past expiration unless USCIS adjudicates and denies earlier, in which case the alien must depart immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable maximum period of stay when Secretary changes determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change in the maximum period of stay announced by Federal Register notice applies to extension of stay or change of status applications filed and pending with USCIS on the effective date of the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange aliens (J) — eligibility and DS-2019 requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A J-1 exchange visitor and accompanying spouse/children may be admitted in J-1/J-2 classifications if each presents a SEVIS Form DS-2019 issued in his/her own name by a program approved by the Department of State; prior to Aug 1, 2003 exigent circumstances allowed a dependent to enter using a copy of the J-1's DS-2019.

rubrics_metrics.name: J admission period relative to program start date
rubrics_metrics.description: An exchange alien and J-2 spouse/children may be admitted up to 30 days before the report date or start of the approved program listed on Form DS-2019; initial admission may not exceed the period specified on DS-2019 plus 30 days for travel or a Commissioner-designated period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A spouse or child may not be admitted for longer than the principal exchange visitor.

rubrics_metrics.name: J readmission rules (IAP-66/Form IAP-66)
rubrics_metrics.description: An exchange alien may be readmitted for the remainder of authorized time on Form I-94 without presenting Form IAP-66 if returning from contiguous foreign territory or adjacent islands after an absence of less than 30 days and presenting the original Form I-94; all other exchange aliens must present a valid Form IAP-66.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An original Form IAP-66 or copy three (pink copy) of a previously issued form presented on return shall be retained by the exchange alien for re-entries during the balance of the stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: J extensions of stay procedure and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: To extend beyond the initial admission period, an exchange alien must apply by submitting a new Form DS-2019 indicating the date to which the program is extended; the extension may not exceed the period specified on DS-2019 plus 30 days for travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions for spouse/children require Form I-94 for each dependent and a list of applicants with personal data; accompanying spouse/child may not receive extension longer than principal.

rubrics_metrics.name: J-2 employment authorization process and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Accompanying spouse and minor children of a J-1 may accept employment only with INS authorization obtained by filing Form I-765 with fee to district director; J-2 employment authorization may be for the duration of the J-1's authorized stay or 4 years, whichever is shorter, and is valid only if the J-1 is maintaining status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Income from J-2 employment may be used to support family's customary activities but will not be authorized if needed to support the J-1 principal. Upon timely-filed extension, only upon approval of extension may J-2 apply for renewal of employment authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of duration of status for J-1 when H-1B numerical cap may be reached
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may, by Federal Register notice, extend the duration of status of any J-1 on behalf of whom an employer has timely filed an application for change of status to H-1B if the H-1B numerical limitation will likely be reached prior to the end of the fiscal year, to complete H-1B adjudication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The alien must not have violated terms of nonimmigrant stay and must not be subject to the 2-year foreign residence requirement at 212(e). Any J-2 dependent similarly benefits. An extension under this paragraph means the J-1 student is considered to be maintaining lawful nonimmigrant status provided they do not violate terms of stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEVIS mandatory issuance requirement for program sponsors
rubrics_metrics.description: At a date to be established by the Department of State (announced in Federal Register), use of the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System (SEVIS) will become mandatory for designated program sponsors; after that date all designated sponsors must begin issuance of SEVIS Form DS-2019.

rubrics_metrics.name: J-1 current name and address reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A J-1 exchange visitor must inform the Service and the responsible officer of the exchange visitor program of any legal name change or change of address within 10 days in a manner prescribed by the program sponsor. For SEVIS-enrolled visitors the responsible officer enters the information into SEVIS within 21 days of notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-SEVIS program visitors must submit change of address to the Service within 10 days. Address must be actual physical residence, not a mailing address, unless the visitor cannot receive mail where residing. If a mailing address is provided, the program must maintain a record of the actual physical location and provide it upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special reporting requirement for graduate medical trainees (Form I-644)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each exchange alien participating in a program of graduate medical education or training shall file Form I-644 annually with the Service attesting to the conditions specified on the form; Form I-644 must also be submitted as an attachment to a completed Form DS-2019 when applying for an extension of stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants in cancelled exchange programs — notice and transition
rubrics_metrics.description: When an exchange visitor program approval is withdrawn, the district director shall send notice to each participant and a copy to the program sponsor. If the exchange visitor is currently engaged in authorized activities, the participant is authorized to remain in the U.S. to engage in those activities until expiration of the previously authorized period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: District director shall notify participants that permission to remain or extension of stay may be obtained if the participant is accepted into another approved program and submits a Form DS-2019 executed by the new sponsor.
